content:
ops-oncall: FYI canary for v2.5.1 started ~10m ago, seeing p95 climb on text-generation route. tagging folks.

deploy-bot: :rocket: Canary rollout started for model-serving v2.5.1 (canary=5%). Metrics: p95 +18% vs baseline, error-rate 0.6%, latency spike around 14:12.

lina: Noticed elevated tail on the same route in staging earlier but thought it was config noise.

ezra: grabbing logs now. can you confirm which pool is serving the canary?

ops-oncall: canary on us-west-2 g4dn pool, traffic split 5/95.

sam: Quick decision checklist: if p95 > 25% or error-rate > 1% for 3 consecutive mins, we auto-trigger deploy-bot rollback. Otherwise manual rollback within 15m.

maya: We should prefer a quick pin for Dedicated customers to 2.5.0 if this propagates — less customer impact.

ops-oncall: Agree. For Hosted: manual rollback first so we can gather traces. For Dedicated: pin.

deploy-bot: Auto-alert threshold: p95 > 150ms sustained 180s OR 5xx rate > 1%. Current p95 is 142ms, baseline 120ms, 5xx 0.6%. Not yet auto.

ezra: Found a small regression in kv-cache eviction that increases token decode time under certain sequence lengths. Patch ready but needs validation.

lina: Can we canary the fix to the same 5% before a full rollout?

sam: Yes, but if we wait too long and p95 drifts into auto threshold we lose control. Ops, do you want me to escalate the canary to 15% to get faster signal?

ops-oncall: Not yet. We'll watch for 5 more minutes. If it crosses our manual criteria we rollback.

(status-bot): Incident note created: INC-2026-045. Assigned: eng-oncall, eng-runtime.

maya: I'll prepare short comms for support and the status page. If we rollback, note that dedicated customers were pinned to 2.5.0 and hosted API reverted to safe path.

ops-oncall: If we decide to rollback, use this command:
```
./deploy rollback --env=prod --service=model-serving --to-version=2.5.0 --reason="canary p95 regression" --tag=manual
```

ops-oncall: Also run this to pin dedicated:
```
./deploy pin-version --env=dedicated --service=model-serving --version=2.5.0 --duration=48h
```

deploy-bot: Canary metrics at +6m: p95 148ms, 5xx 0.9%. Still under auto threshold but trending.

ezra: I'm going to push the kv-cache fix to canary job id 8623. ETA 8 min validation.

sam: If fix fails validation, we do manual rollback and notify customers. I'll prep the rollback comms now.

ops-oncall: OK team — agreed plan: wait max 12 minutes for fix validation. If p95 >= 160ms or 5xx >= 1.2% before then, we execute manual rollback using the command above and pin Dedicated. Maya, post to status page and support. Ezra, post validation results here.

maya: On it. Draft support blurb: "We're observing degraded latency on text-generation. We are reverting the canary and will update when resolved. ETA 30–60m."

deploy-bot: Canary update +12m: p95 163ms, 5xx 1.3% — crossing manual threshold. Recommended action: manual rollback.

ops-oncall: Executing manual rollback now.

ops-oncall: Running rollback command...
```
./deploy rollback --env=prod --service=model-serving --to-version=2.5.0 --reason="canary p95 regression" --tag=manual
```

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: Rollback to 2.5.0 succeeded, traffic restored to baseline split. Post-rollback canary metrics will follow.

status-bot: Status page updated: "Investigating -> Degraded performance" -> "Degraded performance -> Resolved (partial)". Notes: canary for v2.5.1 rolled back; Dedicated pinned to 2.5.0.

ezra: I'll cut the kv-cache fix into a hotfix branch and run extended staging tests. Will request a new canary after validation.

maya: Support copy sent, customer-facing note queued.

ops-oncall: Closing this thread once post-rollback telemetry is stable for 10m. Thanks all. :heart:
